title: Transport workers: roads, ports and docks
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Bharatiya Parivahan Mazdoor Mahasangh, Private Transport Mazdoor Mahasangh and the Port & Dock federation.
body:
BMS lists several federations in transport: the **Bharatiya Parivahan Mazdoor Mahasangh** (road transport undertakings), the **Bharatiya Private Transport Mazdoor Mahasangh** (private operators' workers) and the **Bharatiya Port & Dock Mazdoor Mahasangh**.

## Road transport

State road transport undertakings carry crores of passengers and employ drivers, conductors and mechanics. Issues include **pensions**, **wage revision**, **fleet shortages** and the entry of private operators.

## Private transport

Truck, bus and taxi drivers and their helpers are mostly in the unorganised sector. The questions: fixed duty hours, overtime, insurance, medical care, and safe working conditions on long routes.

## Ports and docks

Ports are national gateways. Dock workers are covered by wage boards and special laws, and the **Dock Workers' Act** is part of the OSH Code. Issues include containerisation, mechanisation, the status of the **dock labour boards** and the effect of port privatisation on job security.

## Transport is life

Whether on a bus, a truck or a ship, the transport worker moves the economy. When he works long hours without rest, the public is at risk as well. For this reason, BMS says that **duty-hour rules and safety** are matters of public interest.
